tasks.instruction: Return the 6-bit field stored in bits 4 through 9 of the input.
tasks.note: Start masks only 5 bits; the wrong edit shifts by 5.

tasks.instruction: Pack the low byte of the first argument into bits 8 to 15 and the low byte of the second argument into bits 0 to 7.
tasks.note: The helper masks to a byte; the shift amount is the bug.

tasks.instruction: Count how many of the eight 4-bit nibbles of the input are nonzero.
tasks.note: Start skips the top nibble; the wrong edit runs nine steps and re-counts nibble 0 because shifts use the low five bits.

tasks.instruction: Return true when bits 28 to 31 of the input hold the value 5 and bits 0 to 7 are not all zero.
tasks.note: Start reads the nibble at bit 24; the wrong edit reads at bit 27.

tasks.instruction: Return the array with slot k (the second argument) replaced by the element that follows it; the slot after the last one is the first.
Count the elements whose two lowest bits equal the two lowest bits of the second argument, comparing only those two bits on both sides.
tasks.note: Both the element and the key need masking.

tasks.instruction: Return a record of the low 16 bits of the input and whether any of the high 16 bits are set.
tasks.note: Start misses a high half equal to exactly 1.

tasks.instruction: The function should return a mask with n bits set starting at bit lo (lo is the first argument, n the second), but it sets only the single bit just above that window. Fix it.
tasks.note: n = 32 shifts by 0 under the five-bit rule, so that mask is 0.

tasks.instruction: Combine the four elements with exclusive-or, after shifting each element left by its index.
tasks.note: or and add agree with xor only when the shifted values share no bits.

tasks.instruction: Set flag k (the second argument, taken modulo 8) in the flags word when the third argument is true, and clear it when it is false.
Advance the counter by one; when the advanced value is exactly 10 it becomes 0, any other value is kept. Right now the counter resets one step too early.
tasks.note: Values above 10 keep counting (wrapping); the wrong edit resets them.

tasks.instruction: Return the input's bytes as an array: bits 16-23, bits 8-15, bits 0-7, then bits 24-31, each field a full 8 bits wide.
The function should report whether two neighbouring elements are equal, but it also compares the last element with the first. Make it compare only true neighbours.
tasks.note: Index i+1 wraps modulo 4 at the last step.

tasks.instruction: Scale both arguments with the helper, then put the scaled first value in the upper 16 bits and the scaled second value, cut to 16 bits, in the lower 16 bits.
tasks.note: The helper is x*3>>2 with a wrapping multiply.

tasks.instruction: The function currently counts set bits among bits 0 to 7, but it should count the positions i from 0 to 7 where bits i and i+1 are both set. Change the helper accordingly.
tasks.note: Pairs overlap; position 7 looks at bit 8.

tasks.instruction: Return the word with bits 8 to 15 replaced by the low 8 bits of the second argument; all other bits of the word stay unchanged.
tasks.note: Start keeps only the field instead of clearing it, and does not mask the value.
